headline: High-risk default interaction: Open Interpreter can read/write the shared filesystem and execute shell commands, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure with dexter's autonomous networked workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and uses autonomous execution, while Open Interpreter can read the filesystem, use clipboard/stdin, and execute code. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if dexter outputs are copied into Open Interpreter or shared via files. No direct shared channel is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF dexter outputs are copied into Open Interpreter via .dexter/scratchpad/ or clipboard, attacker-controlled text can be interpreted as instructions.
IF Open Interpreter is run with --auto_run, injected content can be executed without per-block confirmation.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable Open Interpreter auto-run.
Manually review any dexter-generated text before pasting it into Open Interpreter.
Use a read-only handoff file for any shared content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress to multiple APIs, while Open Interpreter can read the entire local filesystem and also egress to model providers. If dexter artifacts or secrets land in the shared filesystem, Open Interpreter can ingest them and transmit them onward. The pair therefore creates a realistic exfiltration path in default setups.
conditions: IF dexter stores financial data or secrets in .dexter/scratchpad/, Open Interpreter can read them from the shared filesystem.
IF Open Interpreter sends prompts or file contents to configured model providers, those contents may leave the local machine.
mitigations: Store sensitive dexter outputs outside any shared directory.
Restrict Open Interpreter to a dedicated non-sensitive workspace.
Rotate any API keys that may have been written to shared files.
Disable network egress for one agent during sensitive runs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Open Interpreter can write the filesystem and modify git state while dexter can run multiple instances and uses autonomous execution. Shared mutable state via filesystem makes concurrent writes and repository drift plausible. The overlap is not proven to be the same directory, so I keep this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or workspace, concurrent writes can clobber each other.
IF Open Interpreter modifies git state while dexter is generating artifacts, repository history can diverge.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories.
Serialize access to any shared git repository.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Pause one agent before the other writes to disk.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter is autonomous and can emit research outputs, while Open Interpreter can act on files and execute shell commands. If Open Interpreter treats dexter's output as authoritative, it can turn a mistaken research result into an irreversible local action or networked side effect. The pairwise pathway is direct enough to warrant high severity.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes dexter-generated text as instructions or facts without verification, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to execute shell commands from that output, errors can become immediate system changes.
mitigations: Require human review before any Open Interpreter action based on dexter output.
Use a verification step that cross-checks dexter claims against sources.
Disable shell execution for handoff runs.
Limit dexter outputs to summaries, not commands.
requires-engineering: implement typed handoff contracts between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly handles financial data and market data, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine and broad filesystem contents. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if regulated data is stored locally or forwarded to model providers. I do not cite only one agent because the risk depends on both the data class and the local-accessing executor.
conditions: IF regulated financial records are stored in the shared local filesystem, Open Interpreter may process them outside the intended retention boundary.
IF model-provider calls are enabled for Open Interpreter, locally stored regulated data may be transmitted to third parties.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Open Interpreter workspaces.
Review retention settings for any model providers used by Open Interpreter.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive runs by directory.
Delete temporary files after each session.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing.
